about: Screens the UI tests take and the comparison checks, by name. tolerance is the percentage of pixels that may change; the blinking caret alone changes about 0.006%. A screen can set its own tolerance, and ignore, a list of [left, top, right, bottom] rectangles; the two zh Text screens ignore where macOS may show its input source bubble under the caret. Screens in notCompared change from run to run on their own.

notCompared.Full window: After the card expands, replies render again at the new width and the scroll position depends on how long that takes.
notCompared.Editing a long question: The test scrolls inside the edit box; where its text lands depends on the scroll's momentum.
notCompared.zh Approval: The arc around the reply mark turns, and the approval card is caught partway through sliding in.
notCompared.Command approval: The arc around the reply mark turns while the command waits.
notCompared.Loading: The arc around the reply mark turns.
notCompared.Scrolling: Taken while the scroll bar shows; it fades on a timer.
notCompared.After scrolling: Taken as the scroll bar fades.
notCompared.Menu bar menu: Shows the system menu bar, whose clock and items change.
notCompared.Menu bar while open: Shows the system menu bar, whose clock and items change.
notCompared.Menu bar: Shows the system menu bar, whose clock and items change.
